Subject: Load test summary & next steps for Dedicated pool

Rohan —

Thanks again for standing up the test cluster last week. Diego and I pushed a two-hour synthetic run that mimics our production traffic (mostly 1.5–2k request bursts with occasional 8–10k spikes when batch jobs kick off). I attached the TPS CSV and a small set of traces we captured. Topline:

- Avg sustained TPS during peak window: ~2,200
- 99th p50/p95 latency patterns in the CSV — there are a few tail events around 1.2s
- KV cache hit rate currently low because our clients have a wide prompt variety

We want to get a proposal for a reserved GPU pool with throughput guarantees and committed monthly spend. Marcus & Monica mentioned you could help finalize a mutual action plan and pricing tiers.

Questions:
1) Based on the attached traces, how many A100-equivalent GPUs would you recommend for a committed pool to keep p95 < 800ms at 2.5k sustained TPS?
2) What's the pricing delta if we commit to a 12-month reserved pool vs. month-to-month?
3) Any suggestions for config changes (batching, KV caching) that would reduce our unit cost?

Diego, procurement copied — Samira will follow up with procurement if the proposal looks good.

Thanks,
Samira
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme AI

Samira —

Appreciate the test artifacts. I pulled the CSV and had engineering start an initial pass on traces. High-level answers first, then I'll get you a short formal proposal with options and pricing this week:

1) Recommendation: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs for a committed pool to hit your 2.5k sustained TPS target with p95 headroom (we're seeing that configuration handle your trace profiles with batching enabled).
2) Pricing delta: rough ballpark is ~18–22% discount for a 12-month reserved commit vs. on-demand dedicated monthly usage; exact depends on commit size and burst policy.
3) Config suggestions: prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, enable dynamic batching with 12–15ms micro-batch windows, and a token-budget enforcement on long prompts. Neha will drop a short note with numbers.

I'll draft the proposal (two SKUs: 4x reserved pool and 6x reserved pool with burst credits) and share it by EOD Monday. If procurement needs paperwork earlier, let me know and I can route it.

—Rohan

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2024 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Load test analysis (4x vs 6x) — p95 & cost estimates

Folks —

I pulled the traces and ran them through our perf harness (attached trace samples + local run). Key findings:

- 4x A100-equivalent pool: sustained 2.5k TPS achievable with dynamic batching; observed p95 ~ 680–760ms depending on prompt length mix. Token cost per 1k responses approx $0.95.
- 6x pool: p95 drops to ~420–500ms, token cost per 1k responses increases ~40% but gives much more headroom for spikes.
- We saw 3 major tail contributors: long-context requests (>2k tokens), cold KV cache, and unoptimized client-side retries.

Operational recommendations:
- Commit to 4x with a burst policy (up to 6x) and strict burst credits accounting — this gives you latency SLO while keeping committed cost down.
- Add a small prefix cache (client-side hints) — this reduced tokens by ~7% in the sim.

I attached a CSV with the p50/p95 numbers and a ZIP of trace artifacts. Happy to jump on a quick call with Acme infra to walk through a few traces.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: tps_report_2024-04-15.csv; trace_samples_4xA100.zip

Quick update after today's replay: we ran the 2-hour nightly batch spike (I kicked it off at 15:00 PT) and linked the run dashboard: https://redwood.app/dashboards/acme-loadtest-2024 (shared above). Key outcomes:

- 4x reserved pool with configured burst to 6x maintained p95 < 780ms across the replay, with short spike tail events at 95–110s mark driven by three long-context jobs.
- Burst accounting: credits are pooled monthly and roll over for up to three months (per proposal); we can change to annual pooling with procurement if preferred — that would move pricing slightly (I put two examples in the updated proposal PDF).
- Payment terms: net 60 is acceptable for 12-month committals; for 24-month commit we can stretch the discount to 25% and include 1 additional tuning engagement in month 2.

Next steps:
1) I'll upload the final replay artifacts to the Drive folder and share an inviite for a 30-min walkthrough early next week.
2) If procurement is comfortable, we can circulate a redline of the SOW/contract and target an effective start date of May 15.

Thanks — appreciate the fast feedback.
